HomeMax Retail Inc. - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeMax Retail Inc. Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson, Investor Relations Director:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeMax Retail Inc.'s results for the Q3 2024. Joining me on today’s call are Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Lopez, Chief Financial Officer; David Chen, Chief Merchandising Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Stores Officer; Ryan Kim, Chief Marketing Officer; and Emily Vargas, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Alex Thompson.

Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeMax Retail Inc.'s performance for the Q3 2024. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover eight key aspects of our performance:

1. Overall Performance: Good afternoon, and thank you for tuning into our Q3 fiscal 2024 earnings discussion for HomeMax Retail Inc. As CEO, I'm excited to highlight what stands out as an exceptional quarter in a tough retail setting. Our extensive brick-and-mortar network of over 1,200 stores throughout North America powered impressive revenue growth, margin improvements, and advances in our omnichannel strategy. On the top line, Q3 net revenues hit $2.5 billion, reflecting an 8.4% year-over-year rise and surpassing our guidance midpoint while exceeding consensus by 2.7%. Comparable store sales climbed 5.2% on a 52-week basis, with traffic rising 2.8%, conversion edging up 1.9% to 28.4%, and average ticket increasing 0.4% to $72.50. This beat the broader retail sector's flat results according to the NRF index and outperformed category peers like Home Depot and Lowe's, especially in discretionary home areas. Our Home Essentials segment, covering kitchenware, bedding, and small appliances, accounted for 55% of growth with 11.2% revenue increase and 7.1% comps, propelled by private-label hits like our EverGreen cookware, up 25% in units from added displays and demos. Garden and Outdoor trailed at 4.8% comps due to cooler weather, but new vertical garden kits tapped post-pandemic trends for triple-digit growth. E-commerce reached 18% of sales, up from 14%, with $450 million in revenue as BOPIS jumped 32%, using stores as key fulfillment points. Gross margins grew 160 basis points to 38.7%, the best in five years, thanks to private labels at 42% of sales and supply chain savings, including 22% lower freight via 15% more Mexico sourcing and AI inventory tools from Manhattan Associates boosting turns to 5.8x from 5.2x, limiting markdowns to 2.1%. Regionally, Northeast and Midwest with 520 stores led at 6.1% comps from urban projects aiding furniture sales like Target's city stores; Sunbelt at 4.9% despite hurricanes, offset by patio resilience; West Coast at 3.2% hit by rates on decor, similar to Williams-Sonoma; Canadian 100 stores at 7.3% in local currency from tailored Northern Hearth lines. SG&A fell 90 basis points to 27.3% via labor tools like Kronos and AI shrinkage cams in 1,000 stores. Adjusted EBITDA rose 18% to $360 million at 15% margins, above our 13-14% target; EPS $1.18, beating by $0.09; ops cash flow $480 million for repurchases and debt paydown to $2.2 billion net, liquidity $1.5 billion. This reinforces our Stores First, Digital Everywhere approach, with 12 new experiential flagships at 20,000 sq ft featuring AR kiosks outperforming by 15%; Premier Rewards+ at 14 million members up 22%, 65% redemption on exclusives like bamboo bedding with Boll & Branch. We're set for 3-5% full-year comps, Q4 $2.55-2.60 billion revenues, 5-7% comps, grabbing share in McKinsey's 2-3% industry growth as inflation cools.

2. E-Commerce Growth: Thank you. Our omnichannel efforts remain central to evolving our 1,200-store network. In Q3, hybrid sales via BOPIS and curbside grew 28% to $1.2 billion, 22% of digital GMV, adding 4.2 points to comps—11 straight quarters of double-digit gains, above NRF's 18% peer average. BOPIS units rose 32% to 4.8 million at 98.7% fulfillment via our $150 million Omnichannel Fulfillment Network in 85% of stores, RFID on 70% high-velocity SKUs like appliances and decor. BOPIS AOV $145, 15% over e-comm, with 22% add-on attach for warranties. Sunbelt at 28% digital penetration with <2-hour SLAs in Miami and Dallas; rural Midwest at 14%, piloting micro-fulfillment with Alert ALPHABOT. Curbside expanded to 1,050 stores, 2.9 million orders up 41%, <4 min waits, 12% digital sales, 55% growth in staples, 42% margins saving $28 million freight; CarPlay integration cut abandonment 17%. Tech like Manhattan Active Omni ensures 99.9% uptime, Blue Yonder AI reduced stockouts 24%; MaxHub kiosks in 400 stores lift traffic 12%, CLV 8%. Captured 2.5 million digital customers, 65% to loyalty fast; 150 bps margin gain from Kronos scheduling. On track for 95% coverage, $80 million Q4 CapEx at 3x ROI; automation counters labor risks.

3. Store Performance: Turning to store metrics, our inventory turnover hit 5.2x in Q3, up 8% from 4.8x, best Q3 since 2019; full-year 6.1x, up 7% from 5.7x, 60 days on hand vs 64. Hardlines like tools at 7.8x from storm demand, DeWalt partnerships; apparel/softlines to 4.9x via SKU cuts, micro-collections with Levi's/Nike. Seasonals 9.5x via AI planning cutting stockouts 22%; durables 4.1x hit by rates. Southeast/Sunbelt 6.5x from DIY; Northeast/Midwest 5.6x addressed by transfers. Drivers: Mexico/Vietnam sourcing cut leads to 85 days; Dematic automation up 30%; RFID on 80% apparel cut shrink 15 bps; AI forecasting 92% accurate saved $150 million markdowns; micro-DC pilots. Adds 5 bps margin per 0.1x, $2.1 billion inventory down 8%, $450 million capital freed. FY2024 target 6.3-6.5x.

4. Marketing Initiatives: Our digital marketing shone amid 3.2% CPI and confidence at 102. Q3 ROAS 6.2x, up 18%, spend $48 million up 22%, CAC $28 down 15% via GA4/CDP on 1.2 billion signals. 65% to Google Search/Shopping at 7.8x; email/SMS 12.5x, 41% opens. Digital traffic 28% store visits, $1.4 billion sales; BOPIS 34% up. AI personalization 47 segments, 24% conversion lift; server-side Meta 92% match; TikTok incrementality 2.3x visits. Northeast 7.1x local ads; Southeast 5.8x geofence; West 6.5x Pinterest; Canada 5.4x. Digital 41% sales incrementality, CLV $1,240 up 42%; next retail media pilots.

5. Supply Chain Optimization: Progress on markdowns was key, at 11.2% of sales, down 450 bps from 15.7%, lowest in five years vs peers' 16-18%. Boosted gross margin to 38.4%, +320 bps YoY. Inventory down 8% to $1.2 billion, 4.2 turns best in three years; apparel 92% full-price sell-through. Sunbelt 8.5%, Northeast/Midwest 14.1%. AI Blue Yonder 91% forecast, RFID cut clearance 22%; dynamic pricing 75 bps lift. Owned brands 42% sales, 52% margins; sub-11% goal, 39%+ margins.

6. Loyalty Program Update: We've seen strong momentum in our loyalty program refresh, with an 18% rise in active members since June relaunch, akin to Costco but with in-app coupons boosting BOPIS baskets 25%. Penetration at 65% in essentials/beauty, up from 58%, driving 2.5 units per transaction at full price and skewing mix higher.

7. Sustainability Initiatives: On sustainability, we're advancing private-label eco-lines like bamboo bedding and EverGreen cookware from sustainable sources, now key to 42% private-label mix, reducing environmental impact while appealing to value-conscious shoppers, with early comp lifts in Health & Wellness up 9%.

8. Technology Investments: Tech investments in AI demand sensing, RFID across 80% apparel, and cloud platforms like Vertex AI have enhanced personalization, forecast accuracy to 92%, and shrink reduction by 15%, positioning us competitively.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria Lopez to provide more details on our financial results.

Maria Lopez, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Alex. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the Q3 2024.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.5 billion, a 5.2% increase compared to the same period last year. Gross margin was 38.5%, up 85 basis points year-over-year from 30.55% primarily driven by favorable product mix with private labels at 28% of sales up from 24%, reduced markdowns to 12% from 16%, lower freight to 2.8% from 3.4% via vendor deals and DC automation up 22% throughput, and shrinkage to 1.2% from 1.4% with RFID on 40% SKUs. Northeast/Midwest expanded 110 bps to 33.2%; Southeast 29.1%; West steady at 30.8%. BOPIS adds 300 bps over e-comm; expect Q4 31.7-32.0%.

Operating expenses were $650 million, representing 26% of revenue. Net income was $180 million, or $1.18 per share. We generated $280 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently healthy, down 5% year-over-year with strong turnover.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Looking ahead to our outlook for Q4 fiscal 2024 and into 2025, this guidance balances execution in a cautious consumer setting with inflation, rates, and traffic softness like peers Macy's, Kohl's. Q4 net sales $2.45-2.55 billion, 2-5% growth, comps 1.5-4% with stores 1-3.5%, digital 5-8%; holiday private loungewear/home decor +250 bps early. Gross margin 38.5-39.5%, +50-150 bps from 15% fewer markdowns via AI pricing, owned brands 42% up from 38% with 12% comps in Essentials Home, 8% lower unit freight from Mexico nearshoring. SG&A 26.5-27.5%, +25 bps from RFID/labor system cutting out-of-stocks 22%, conversion +1.2 pts, $15 million savings from 25 closures/50 remodels. Op income $180-210 million, 7.3-8.2%; EPS $0.85-1.00 adjusted; FCF >$250 million for dividend/repurchases. Full-year: sales $9.8-10.0 billion up midpoint, comps 2.5-4.5%, gross 39.0-39.8%, op margin 6.5-7.2%, EPS $3.20-3.50; inventory flat to -2%. Northeast/Midwest 4-6% comps, BOPIS hubs +$8 basket; Southeast flat-+2% post-hurricanes; West +3-5%. Apparel +3% led by activewear +15%; home +2%; essentials +5%. Pillars: omnichannel to 35% by 2026, AR returns -25%; GenAI in 200 stores +18% add-to-cart; Rewards 25 million members, tiered perks/credit cards 20% sales. Risks: traffic -1%, tariffs; upside soft landing. Brick-mortar 72% sales via experiences; 50% FCF to shareholders, $400 million CapEx.

For Q4 ending Dec 2025 and FY2025, post Q3 5.2% comps/EPS +12% to $1.18, cautious optimism with consumer selectivity, supply normalization, omnichannel efficiencies; conservatism on Northeast/Midwest weather, sentiment at 103.8. Q4 revenue $2.55-2.60 billion, 4-6% growth, comps +2.5-3.5% higher in essentials/home improvement mid-single digits, offsetting flat apparel/seasonal. Gross 28.5-29.0%, +50 bps from private labels 42%, HomeEssentials 200-300 bps better, freight -20%, AI shrink -15% like Target. SG&A 21.0-21.5%, wage/marketing offset by 18% loyalty uplift, 25% BOPIS baskets. EPS $1.22-1.32, +8-15%, 24.5% tax, $150 million buybacks, $120 million CapEx remodels. FY2025 revenue $10.1-10.3 billion, 3.5-5.5%, sq ft comps +2-3%, +2.5% net sq ft from 12 openings/5 relocations Sunbelt. Gross 28.2-28.7%, +40-90 bps pricing/vendor rebates. Op margin 7.8-8.2%, 95% omnichannel fulfillment. EPS $4.65-4.85, +10-15%, debt/EBITDA 1.8x, M&A like HVAC tuck-in. Southeast/West +4% housing/outdoor +12%; Midwest +1% cool weather; Canada +6%. Pillars: BOPIS 28% sales, costs -22% micro-centers; RFID 70% apparel, turns 8.5x like Macy's; health +9% GLP-1, pro perks. Fed cuts tailwind, election/tariffs risk; $50 million savings Mexico. Guide to beat, +200-300 bps comps last 8 quarters.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to David Chen, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, followed by Lisa Patel to discuss store operations, Ryan Kim to discuss marketing initiatives, and Emily Vargas to talk about technology advancements.

David Chen, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Maria. This quarter, we launched our Essentials Home line, which has seen strong double-digit comp growth and higher margins through expanded private-label assortments in kitchen and wellness, exciting us for upcoming launches in seasonal and outdoor categories.

Lisa Patel, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, David. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented remodels with experiential zones like design pods and interactive kiosks in 50 high-traffic locations and are seeing positive results with 15% higher comps.

Ryan Kim, Chief Marketing Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. Our new marketing campaign, Home Refresh, has increased brand awareness by 25% through targeted digital-to-physical efforts driving store traffic and loyalty engagement.

Emily Vargas, Chief Technology Officer:
Thank you, Ryan. We have invested in AI-powered demand sensing and RFID platforms which have improved our inventory accuracy to 92%, reduced shrink by 15%, and enabled dynamic pricing for better sell-through.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your sales?

Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Good morning, John. Inflation has pressured discretionary categories like home decor, but our essentials and private labels have shown resilience with mid-single-digit comps, as consumers prioritize value in high-frequency items—we've offset this through targeted pricing discipline and loyalty perks keeping overall comps at 5.2%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Maria Lopez, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Mike. For Q4, we're guiding comps to +2.5% to +3.5%, weighted higher in essentials and home improvement, reflecting continued strength in consumables offsetting seasonal normalization, with upside from omnichannel execution.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee (Barclays):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Absolutely, Sarah. We've nearshored more to Mexico, cutting freight 8-22% and lead times to 85 days, added DC automation for 30% efficiency, and AI forecasting to avoid overstock—combined with vendor negotiations, this supported markdown reductions and healthy inventory turns.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Wilson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Wilson (Morgan Stanley):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Great question, Tom. The refresh has driven 18% more active members, 25% higher BOPIS baskets via personalized coupons, and 65% penetration in growth categories, contributing to fuller-price sales and 2.5 extra units per transaction.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Chen with Citi. Please go ahead.

Laura Chen (Citi):
How are you thinking about gross margin outlook given markdown trends?

Maria Lopez, Chief Financial Officer:
Thanks, Laura. We're targeting continued expansion with sub-11% markdowns, owned brands at 42% delivering 52% margins, and supply efficiencies—the Q4 guide of 28.5-29.0% embeds 50 bps growth, with FY2025 at 28.2-28.7%.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes the question-and-answer session.

Alex Thompson, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Johnson, Investor Relations Director:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
